notes: Traces to Jejungwon (1885), founded by Horace N. Allen and rebuilt as Severance Hospital with Louis H. Severance's funding, opened 1904.

name: University Health Network (UHN)
type: Public system — academic health sciences center (Ontario)
ownership_parent: Public hospital corporation under Ontario's Public Hospitals Act; part of Ontario Health
leadership: President and Chief Executive Officer: Kevin Smith, DPhil. Chair, Board of Directors: Dean Connor. (UHN releases, Feb. and Oct. 2026.) CFO/COO/CMO equivalents are published by UHN; not consolidated here — flagged, not guessed.
facilities_scale: Ten sites including Toronto General Hospital, Toronto Western Hospital, Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, Toronto Rehabilitation Institute and the Michener Institute; a workforce of more than 44,000 staff, learners and volunteers in some counts (about 23,000 employees in narrower counts — measures differ and are flagged); 1,250 principal investigators and 5,100 research staff and trainees with $688 million in annual research funding (UHN, Oct. 2026) — Canada's largest hospital-based research enterprise.
specialties: Transplant (Ajmera Transplant Centre, among the world's largest), cardiac care (Peter Munk Cardiac Centre), oncology (Princess Margaret, a top-10 global specialized cancer hospital), neuroscience (Krembil Brain Institute), rehabilitation and complex continuing care; Newsweek World's Best Hospitals 2026 ranked Toronto General No. 2 in the world (UHN, Feb. 2026).
patient_categories: Ontario public-system patients (OHIP), plus national and international referrals for transplant, cardiac and cancer programs; private-pay categories limited under Ontario law.
contact: Official route: hospitals, appointments and contact via uhn.ca. No general published email.
sources: UHN releases via PR Newswire and Business Wire (Feb. 2026; Oct. 13, 2026); UHN institutional pages.
notes: Canada's flagship entry: a public, universal-system operator ranked with the world's best private and nonprofit names.

name: Einstein Hospital Israelita (Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein)
type: Nonprofit (sociedade beneficente) hospital and health system
ownership_parent: Sociedade Beneficente Israelita Brasileira Albert Einstein (nonprofit beneficent society)
leadership: President: Sidney Klajner, M.D. (President of the Sociedade Beneficente Israelita Brasileira Albert Einstein; Einstein and Mayo Clinic releases, 2025–2026). Exact consolidated bed and staff counts vary by source and year and are flagged rather than asserted.
specialties: Latin America's top-ranked hospital (Newsweek: No. 22 worldwide in recent editions, per partner releases): oncology and hematology with the region's first CAR-T and CAR-NK cell therapy programs, cardiology, neurology, transplant, robotic surgery, and a national reference role in digital health and AI (a founding member of Mayo Clinic Platform_Connect).
patient_categories: Private insured and self-pay patients at its own units, and public (SUS) patients at the public hospitals and units Einstein manages under government contracts — a dual role stated in its institutional materials.
contact: Official route: units, appointments and contact via einstein.br. No general published email.
sources: Einstein Hospital Israelita releases via Business Wire (Oct. 2, 2025); Mayo Clinic News Network (2026); Institute for Healthcare Improvement board profile (2026).

name: Rede D'Or Sao Luiz
type: Private (for-profit, publicly traded; B3: RDOR3)
ownership_parent: Rede D'Or Sao Luiz S.A. (public shareholders; controlled by the Moll family with investment funds under a long-term shareholders' agreement reaffirmed in 2026)
leadership: Chairman: Jorge Moll. Chief Executive Officer: Paulo Moll. (Governance and succession agreements reported Oct. 2026, confirming both in role.) CFO and other executive officers are published in Rede D'Or's reference form; not consolidated here — flagged.

An expansion program targets thousands of additional beds through 2028.
specialties: Brazil's largest private hospital network: full-spectrum acute care with noted oncology (a national oncology network), cardiology, neurology, maternity and high-complexity surgery; integrated with SulAmerica health and dental insurance, life insurance and pension products.
patient_categories: Privately insured patients (including SulAmerica beneficiaries), self-pay patients and corporate clients; categories published in company reporting.
contact: Official route: hospitals and contact via rededorsaoluiz.com.br; investor relations at ri.rededor.com.br. No general published email.
sources: Rede D'Or earnings releases and reference form (2025); governance announcement reporting (Oct. 2026).
notes: Founded in 1977 as a cardiology laboratory (Cardiolab) in Rio de Janeiro by Jorge Moll.

name: Sheba Medical Center
type: Public system — government hospital (Israel Ministry of Health)
ownership_parent: State of Israel (government hospital), with the Sheba Medical Center organization operating its 'City of Health' campus
leadership: Director General and Chief Executive Officer: Professor Yitshak Kreiss, M.D. (Sheba releases, 2025–2026). Deputy and CFO/CMO equivalents are published by Sheba in Hebrew and English profiles; not consolidated here — flagged, not guessed.
facilities_scale: A single 'City of Health' campus with seven hospitals and 11 centers of excellence, treating more than 2 million patients a year (Sheba, Feb. 2026); about 2,000 beds and roughly 10,000 staff in hospital-published ranges (dated figures vary — flagged). Newsweek World's Best Hospitals 2026: No. 7 worldwide, its eighth consecutive year in the top ranks (Sheba, 2026).
specialties: Full-spectrum tertiary care with the ARC (Accelerate, Redesign, Collaborate) innovation platform founded at Sheba in 2019 and now spanning more than 30 health systems in a dozen countries; oncology, cardiology, rehabilitation (a national rehabilitation role), pediatrics (Edmond and Lily Safra Children's Hospital), pandemic preparedness (SPRI), and AI and digital health programs with global partners.
patient_categories: Israeli public-system patients through the four national health funds, military and veteran patients (Tel HaShomer origins), and international patients and government-to-government programs.
contact: Official route: departments, international patients and contact via sheba.co.il and sheba-global.com. No general published email.
sources: Sheba Medical Center releases (2025–2026); ARC Global / Redesign Health announcement (Oct. 2026).
notes: Israel's largest hospital, on the Tel HaShomer campus east of Tel Aviv.

name: Aga Khan University Hospitals and Aga Khan Health Services (AKDN Health System)
hq: Karachi, Pakistan (AKU) and Nairobi, Kenya (AKHS East Africa)
type: Nonprofit (Aga Khan Development Network agencies)
ownership_parent: Aga Khan University and Aga Khan Health Services, agencies of the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN)
leadership: President and Vice Chancellor, Aga Khan University: Dr Sulaiman Shahabuddin (AKU Office of the President, 2026). Chief Executive Officer, AKU Health Services, Pakistan: Dr Farhat Abbas (AKU releases). Chief Executive Officer, Aga Khan University Hospital, Nairobi: Rashid Khalani (Kenya Ministry of Health partnership reporting, 2025). Director of Health, AKDN: Dr Gijs Walraven. (AKDN/AKU sources, 2025–2026.) A single group CFO title is not published across the network — stated plainly.
facilities_scale: Aga Khan University Hospitals in Karachi (the 710-bed-class flagship at Stadium Road, JCI-accredited since 2006, with SafeCare Level 5 off-campus hospitals), Nairobi and the new 101-bed Aga Khan University Hospital, Kampala (opened with the AKU Uganda campus, 2025); Aga Khan Health Services operates hospitals and more than 100 health centers across Pakistan, Kenya, Tanzania, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Syria and Kyrgyzstan; AKHS East Africa alone cares for more than 1 million patients a year (AKU presidential biography). System-wide bed and staff totals are not published as one figure — flagged, not assembled.
specialties: University hospital care in low- and middle-income settings: cardiology and cardiac surgery, oncology, kidney transplant, women's and children's health (including the French Medical Institute for Mothers and Children, Kabul), neurology, and primary and community health at scale; a network-wide quality and patient safety system ('One System, One Standard', AKDN Health System Quality Symposium, Nairobi, May 2025).
patient_categories: Private and welfare-supported patients — AKDN institutions publish patient welfare and zakat-supported care programs for patients unable to pay — plus public partnership patients (for example, subsidized kidney transplant and cardiac surgery patients under Kenya's Social Health Authority partnership, 2025).
contact: Official route: hospitals and contact via aku.edu and agakhanhospitals.org. No single general published email across the network.
sources: Aga Khan University Office of the President and news pages (2025–2026); AKDN/AKHS quality symposium release (June 3, 2025); Kenya News Agency (2025).
notes: The broadest geographic nonprofit footprint in this guide, and its clearest example of a provider built for underserved regions.
